body:
# Headless canvas — what exists and what escher can take (the escher overseer's research, 2026-11-18)

Asked by the founder after 0.3.0 closed: «И по хорошему прежде чем стартовать надо ресерчнуть по поводу хедлесс
канваса как что где реализовано, и подумать что мы можем себе взять». Four read-only passes, returned by
2026-11-18 21:54Z: three over the web, one over escher's tree as it stood on disk after `bc7661240`. Each claim
is marked: **[P]** the agent fetched the primary page (through a summarizing fetch, so a quote is its extract),
**[S]** a search summary only, **[code]** read in escher's tree by a read-only agent (no build, no git).
Nothing here was built or run; every code fact is a hypothesis for the phase that touches it to re-measure.

## 1. escher's own ground (code facts; they correct `intent.md` findings 3–7)
- A `<canvas>` is `SpecialElementData::Canvas(CanvasData { custom_paint_source_id: u64 })`
  (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs:372`, `:1012`); the id is parsed from `<canvas src="N">` and
  `canvas_data()` has no caller. `blitz-paint` names `Canvas` nowhere. [code]
- What paints today is the **`Widget` trait** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs:75`):
  `paint(&mut dyn RenderContext, styles, width, height, scale) -> Scene`, registered by
  `doc.mutate().set_custom_widget(node_id, Box<dyn Widget>)`; `blitz-paint` appends the widget's scene
  (`render.rs:615`, `:1377`) behind the `custom-widget` feature. Upstream replaced `CustomPaintSource` with it in
  blitz PR #425 [P]. The path is CPU-safe: a scene fragment, no GPU handle unless the widget downcasts for one.
- **The harness may paint no widget at all:** `packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml:18` takes `blitz-paint` with
  `default-features = false`, which drops `custom-widget`, unless another crate of the build unifies it. Not
  measurable by reading: the FIRST measurement of the version. [code]
- Headless shots: `render_to_buffer::<VelloCpuImageRenderer, _>` (`blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:83`);
  pins `anyrender 0.15.0`, `anyrender_vello_cpu 0.19.0`, `anyrender_serialize 0.9.0` (root `Cargo.toml:121-125`),
  the last used by `apps/browser` alone. [code]
- Reserved already: `Placer::App { canvas }` in the `layout` verb («Reserved: nothing places a node so yet»,
  `packages/escher-driver/src/layout.rs:58`); a commented `accessibility_tree` on `Widget` under «TODO: allow for
  multiple nodes per widget» (`custom_widget.rs:144`); `Harness::drag(from, to, steps)` with `mouse_down_at`,
  `move_mouse_to`, `mouse_up_at` (`blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:112-150`); `Widget::handle_event`. [code]
- Not there: a snapshot node needs an `author_id` AND a DOM element (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:153`),
  so no non-DOM node can appear; the graph reserves no id form for one; the driver has fifteen verbs, none `drag`
  (`command.rs:935,945` pin 15 and `(11, 3, 1)`); no stand app holds a canvas (two engine tests do). [code]
- An action's point is the centre of the snapshot bounds, checked by `visible_region` — «Exact under a translate
  and a scale; under a rotation it reads the bounding box» (`execute.rs:652`, `blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:816`). [code]

## 2. Painting headless on the CPU
- Upstream Blitz has no Canvas 2D context and expects the embedder to bring one (PR #1210, open) [P]; open issue
  #1578: a widget's paint gets the border-box size but is placed at the content-box origin [P].
- `anyrender_vello_cpu` paints `Paint::Custom` / `Paint::Resource` transparent with no warning, ignores backdrop
  filters, and drops layer filters when multithreaded [P] — the dead end is anything routed through a texture.
- **Servo is the one production Canvas2D on `vello_cpu`** (`components/canvas/vello_cpu_backend.rs`): clip stack,
  composite ops as blend layers, `clear_rect`, text as glyph runs. MPL-2.0, tied to Servo's crates — a mapping to
  read, not a crate to take; shadows unimplemented [P].
- Other rasterizers: tiny-skia has no text [P]; raqote and forma are stale [P]; skia-safe is a Skia dependency.
  No standalone native Canvas2D crate was found [S].
- Determinism: nobody claims bit-exact output across architectures. Vello's own tests compare with a tolerance
  [P]; @napi-rs/canvas documents one colour level of difference between x64 and arm64 and makes text portable only
  with registered fonts, full glyph coverage and a fixed language [P]. `vello_cpu` offers an `f32_pipeline`
  «useful for test snapshots» [P]; whether its output varies by SIMD level was not found.

## 3. The canvas read as data
- **Flutter's DisplayList test form is the closest precedent:** one line per op in paint order, layers as
  indentation, equality of two lists [P]. Skia's debugger adds the clip and matrix at each command and a filter by
  command name; `skp_parser` dumps JSON with images and typefaces by reference [P/S].
- WebRender derives its capture from the types through serde; its hand-kept YAML writer «was frequently broken» [P].
- jest-canvas-mock keeps two granularities: every call, and effective draws only [P].
- Excalidraw, tldraw and Konva assert on the object model, never on draw calls [S] — the dump should group by
  logical object.
- Not found anywhere: how large such dumps get, float rounding practice, a diff of two dumps. Ours to measure.

## 4. Virtual nodes, `drag`, pan and zoom
- **Flutter `CustomPainterSemantics`**: the painter returns a list of `{key, rect, properties, transform}` per
  paint [P]. Android's `ExploreByTouchHelper` is the callback form (`getVirtualViewAt`, populate, perform) with
  explicit invalidation, mandatory after an add or a remove [P]. Qt has `isValid()` for a stale object [P].
- **AccessKit carries nodes with no DOM behind them:** `bounds` in the node's space, a `transform` applied to the
  node and its descendants, `is_hidden`, `is_disabled`, `clips_children`; it has no drag action [P].
- The web removed `addHitRegion` because it altered hit testing (whatwg/html PR #1942) [P]; Figma mirrors its
  canvas into a DOM generated from an internal accessibility tree [S]; React Flow and tldraw keep nodes in the DOM
  and only edges or geometry in canvas [P].
- Drivers: Playwright `dragTo(target, {sourcePosition, targetPosition, steps})`, `steps` defaulting to 1, and its
  note that a manual drag needs at least two moves [P]; flutter_test splits a drag in two or the update never
  fires, and has `panZoomStart/Update/End` [P]; WebDriver wheel and pointer moves with `move target out of
  bounds` [P]; kittest drives by accessibility query plus `drag_at` / `drop_at` [P].

## 4a. Upstream's own status page (for 0.5.0's modern-HTML probe; fetched 2026-11-18 22:15Z, the founder's pointer)
`blitz.is/status/css`, `/status/elements`, `/status/events` and roadmap issue #119, read by a fetch agent [P]. It
describes UPSTREAM main, not escher: escher's own `<select>` reads «Not supported» there. Each line is the page's
word, to be measured on escher before it is relied on.
- `position: sticky` — In Progress (blitz#887; the roadmap puts it at 1.0). `fixed`, `absolute`, `z-index` — Supported.
- `scroll-snap-type` / `-align` / `-stop` — Not supported. `overflow: auto` — Not supported (`scroll`, `hidden`,
  `clip` are). `scroll-margin`, `scroll-padding`, `overscroll-behavior` — Not supported.
- Transitions and Animations — Supported. `clip-path`, `mask-*`, `box-shadow`, `opacity`, 2D `transform` —
  Supported (a node with opacity is clipped whatever its overflow). The roadmap still lists clip-path, mask and
  animations as pending: the two pages disagree.
- `filter` — Partial: «Supported with the Skia backend. Partially supported (blur and drop-shadow only) with Vello
  Hybrid.» `backdrop-filter` — Partial: «Supported with the Skia backend.» Neither names the CPU backend our
  headless shots use. `mix-blend-mode`, `background-blend-mode` — Not supported.
- 3D transforms, `perspective`, the individual `scale` / `rotate` / `translate` properties, `transform-box` — Not supported.
- SVG — Partial: static only, no CSS `fill` / `stroke`, no filters. `<canvas>` — «A proprietary API to render a raw
  WGPU texture is supported».
- Events: no drag events, no `ResizeObserver` / `IntersectionObserver` / `MutationObserver`, no `change`, `resize`,
  `load`. Elements: no `dialog`, `progress`, `meter`, `video`, `picture`.
- Subgrid, anchor positioning, multi-column, `content-visibility` — Not supported.

## 5. What the overseer proposes to take (a proposal for the route and its phases, not a decision)
1. **Paint through `Widget::paint -> Scene`, on the pinned `vello_cpu`.** No new rasterizer, no texture path.
   First entry: measure whether the harness paints a widget, and make the stand's canvas fixture show in a shot.
2. **No Canvas 2D context of our own in 0.4.0** unless the founder asks for one: the app paints with anyrender's
   scene API. Servo's backend is the reference if a 2D context is ever wanted.
3. **The read verb prints the recorded scene in Flutter's shape**, generated from `RenderCommand` by serde,
   heavy data by reference, glyph runs as their text, a summary level and a full level, filters by kind and
   region — grouped by virtual node where one covers the commands.
4. **Virtual nodes declared as a per-paint list** `{key, role, name, rect in canvas space, disabled}` beside the
   scene, emitted as AccessKit nodes under the canvas with the canvas's transform; the author key is the id
   (his KEYS + ANCHORS ruling of 2026-10-06); a key gone at action time is a `stale` refusal.
5. **Regions give semantics and refusals; events still go to the widget as ordinary pointer events at the
   resolved point** — the `addHitRegion` lesson.
6. **`drag <src> (to <dst> | by dx,dy)` with several interpolated moves by default**, source and destination
   both checked for refusals first, on the harness's existing primitive. Zoom is its own verb (wheel, pinch).
7. **Determinism stated honestly:** bundled fonts (v030-14), one thread, and a measurement on CI's hosts of
   whether a canvas shot is byte-equal across Linux, macOS and Windows; the data form is the primary observation
   and does not depend on it.

## Forks that look like the founder's (each at its phase, with its measurement)
- A Canvas 2D context (the web API, for page scripts) or anyrender's scene API alone.
- The declaration form: a per-paint list, or callbacks with invalidation.
- What the read verb may carry to a model provider (a boundary widening: authored text in glyph runs).
- Cross-host pixel equality of a canvas: required, or a stated tolerance.

The probe adds `peniko = { workspace = true }` to blitz-tests' dev-dependencies (a one-line `Cargo.lock` move, so the probe ran without `--locked`). Source and logs: `evidence/p3-canvas-probe.rs.txt`, `evidence/p3-probe-{per-package,feature-on,workspace}.log`.
| Build selection | Command (in the worktree) | (50,50) non-incremental | (50,50) incremental | Verdict |
| per package | `cargo test -p blitz-tests --test canvas_probe` | `[255, 255, 255, 255]` | not reached (the first mode's assert panicked) | **red** — the widget is not painted |
| per package + the feature | `cargo test -p blitz-tests --features blitz-paint/custom-widget --test canvas_probe` | `[255, 0, 0, 255]` | `[255, 0, 0, 255]` | green |
| workspace | `cargo test --workspace --test canvas_probe` | `[255, 0, 0, 255]` | `[255, 0, 0, 255]` | green |

(400, 400) read `[255, 255, 255, 255]` in every run. The second row isolates the cause: one feature, `blitz-paint/custom-widget`, decides whether a harness shot paints a widget; the widget, its `<object data>` hand-off through the Dioxus mutation writer and the stand boot are otherwise identical. The workspace run's manifests were resolved at its launch, before the option-A reading below edited the worktree's harness manifest (edit 03:33:25 local, the run's log closed 03:33:40; the harness manifest was restored after).

**Option A measured (the harness takes the feature):** with only `packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml`'s `blitz-paint` line given `features = ["custom-widget"]`, `cargo tree --locked -e features -i blitz-paint --depth 1` reads `custom-widget` for `-p blitz-test-harness`, `-p escher-driver` and `-p seven_guis`, the `--locked` read passing (no lock move of its own; the worktree's one lock line is the probe's `peniko`); `cargo tree --locked -p seven_guis -e normal --prefix none | sort -u` reads 479 lines at HEAD and 479 with the change, and `^accesskit_(xplat|winit) ` 0 rows.

# Founder forks — 2026-11-23-canvas-in-a-headless-shot («Canvas in a headless shot», v040-09)

Written at P4 of the take-up (run `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-23T02-07-37-phase/`), on the operator's directive
(`inputs#I1`): every fork that is the operator's — a boundary widening, a new carrier, verb, crossing or public
surface, a choice that turns what the canvas is — is written here, none answered by a default. The plan is not
written yet; it waits on these words. Technical forks go to the operator as dialogs, not here.

## What was measured first, on the stand (the ground every fork below stands on)
A throwaway probe in a detached worktree of HEAD `ac8e6d58a` (session scratchpad, never this tree) boots through
the stand's own `stand::boot_alone` an `<object data>` whose widget paints a red rectangle from Rust, takes
`Harness::screenshot`, and reads the pixel inside it. Evidence beside this file: `p3-canvas-probe.rs.txt`,
`p3-probe-{per-package,feature-on,workspace}.log`.

| Build | Pixel inside the widget | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo test -p blitz-tests` (per package — how `stand-repeat`, `escher-session` and `just seven_guis` build) | `[255, 255, 255, 255]` — white | **red**: the widget is not painted |
| the same + `--features blitz-paint/custom-widget` | `[255, 0, 0, 255]`, both layout modes | green |
| `cargo test --workspace` (CI's `test` leg) | `[255, 0, 0, 255]`, both layout modes | green |

So today a canvas shows in a shot or not depending only on which packages a cargo command selected. The fix the
plan leans to (the harness names `blitz-paint/custom-widget`) was read with `cargo tree --locked`: it turns the
feature on for `blitz-test-harness`, `escher-driver` and `seven_guis` — and so for `escher-session` and the
windowed `seven_guis_native` too — adds no package (`seven_guis`' graph 479 lines before and after) and no
platform adapter (0 rows). Which fix to take is a technical fork, asked as a dialog.

**A fact both forks depend on:** none of the seven served tasks holds a widget today, and no served app paints
one. Whatever is ruled below, nothing app-painted crosses a carrier until a served app holds a canvas («Circle
Drawer on a canvas» is the first route entry that would). And in a **workspace** build the driver already paints a
widget today (row 3 above) — the crossing is latent in the tree as it stands, reached by no served app.

---

## Fork F1 — a canvas's app-painted content leaves as pixels through `screenshot`

**What crosses.** What an app paints into a canvas from Rust — shapes, colours and, from the next entry on, text
the app draws (labels, values) — leaves the process as pixels inside a `screenshot` answer: base64 PNG in the JSON
line on the session socket and the command line's stdout, an `image` block on the `mcp` role's stdout, and from
there, on a cold-agent live run, to the model provider in the transcript. It does **not** reach a kept check: a
shot is kept as `{"width","height"}` without its pixels (architecture `decision/kept-check-masking`,
security-plan `decision/kept-check-answer-whole`), and no committed check holds a `screenshot` step. No new
carrier, verb, field, exit, cause, log field or span: the shot's own fields are unmoved.

**The rule of ours it meets.**
- security-plan `decision/boundary-widening-rule` / `decision/closed-value-field-no-widening`: a new field of a
  closed value set inside a ratified carrier is no widening; authored text or an open value set still is.
  App-painted pixels are an open value set, and canvas text the app draws is authored text.
- Playbook escalate pattern `rul-izni57qv` («Boundary widening — … a validated surface admits a new input class
  …»): always a human's call; the wrap halts on it.
- The precedent: an open select list's option and group labels leaving as pixels in a shot was put to the founder
  and ratified as a widening (security-plan `decision/open-list-shot-pixels`, architecture
  `decision/select-list-crossing`), though no field moved. A canvas's content is a content class of its own.
- The intent's principle «Observe the canvas as data, not pixels» (the founder, 2026-10-29): «Screenshots stay for
  people and visual questions» — it keeps shots, it does not decide what a shot of a canvas may carry out.

**Options, with their measured cost.**
- **A — Ratify: a canvas's painted content crosses as pixels in a shot on every ratified carrier**, the shot's
  fields unmoved, as the select list's labels do. Code cost: none beyond the fix (the harness feature line, one
  test target). Record cost: one security-plan decision row and one architecture crossing row in the wrap's
  amendments, under `rul-izni57qv` (the wrap halts once, as the answer card). The capability statement
  (`docs/capabilities.md`) names it when v040-09 is claimed. Nothing crosses today (no served app holds a canvas).
- **B — Ratify for the in-process and local carriers only, not the model provider**: the socket, the command line
  and MCP carry it; the cold-agent live run may not reach a canvas app until a later ruling. Code cost now: none
  (no served app holds a canvas, no live run is planned in this chunk). Cost later: «Cold-agent live run»
  (v040-15) names «the two canvas samples among its apps» — that entry would need this ruling reopened.
- **C — Keep a canvas's content off the carriers: a shot taken through the driver paints no widget**, while
  in-process harness checks do. Measured: this cannot be done by feature selection — a workspace build unifies
  the feature on for the driver too (row 3 above) — so it needs a runtime switch the driver sets on its harness
  (a new `Harness` option or a paint flag, an escher change to `paint_scene`'s widget pass or to the harness's
  `paint_viewport`), one new closed difference between an in-process shot and a carrier shot, and a check of it.
  It contradicts the route's «Circle Drawer on a canvas» (whose acceptance reads «a shot of Circle Drawer shows the
  circles») and v040-09's acceptance on the carriers.
- **D — Defer the ruling: this chunk lands the harness and stand witness only, and states the crossing as
  unruled** — the fix still makes the driver paint widgets in every build (it rides the harness), so the latent
  crossing becomes reachable by any app booted per package; nothing served holds one. The ruling moves to «Circle
  Drawer on a canvas». Cost: a residual row naming the open crossing; the wrap records it PROVISIONAL.

**Dependences.** F2 B (serve a canvas page) requires F1 A or B — a served page puts the content on the carriers
at once. F1 C changes the technical fix's shape (the dialog's options assume the driver paints widgets).
The next entry, «Canvas placement and text», adds canvas text from the bundled fonts: under A that text crosses as
pixels too, so A ratifies text the app draws into a canvas as well, not shapes alone.

---

## Fork F2 — does the stand serve a canvas page on the carriers in this chunk?

**What crosses.** If served: a new app name in `escher-session start <task>`, the usage line's `apps:` and the MCP
`start` tool's `enum` (one private table, architecture `decision/session-apps-one-table`) — a new item of a
closed served-task list, which the order page's addition (2026-11-18-served-error-page) took as a ruled boundary
item — and the page's screens (its snapshot, lint, graph, actions, layout answers and shots) on every carrier.
If not served: nothing; the page is booted in process by the stand checks alone, like `stand::boot_alone`
(architecture `absence/component-alone-on-carriers`).

**The rule of ours it meets.** Architecture `decision/new-carrier-widens-boundary` and the served-task rows
(`contract/escher-session-served-tasks/*`, `contract/escher-session/invocation` «the stand's seven served tasks»);
the route entry asks for a measurement «on the stand first», which an in-process stand boot meets.

**Options, with their measured cost.**
- **A — In process only (lean of the route's own order)**: the stand check boots the canvas through
  `stand::boot_alone` (or a `stand::boot_*` beside `boot_cells` and `boot_load`), on no carrier. Cost: one new
  `stand_` target; 0 served-count sites move; F1's crossing stays latent. «Circle Drawer on a canvas» is where a
  served canvas first appears (Circle Drawer is not served today either).
- **B — Serve a `canvas` page now**: cost measured by `git grep -c -i -E "seven served|seven tasks"` outside
  `.andromeda`: 33 hits in 16 files to sweep (docs, CLAUDE.md, the capability statement's five places, five stand
  checks, `cli_commands`, `cold-agent.sh`); one row in the served table; `stand_cross_os_readings`' committed
  digest table re-recorded on Linux, macOS and Windows CI; the cold-agent apps count; the page's lint-at-boot,
  contrast and Tab-order rows (a11y history: a served page without them is a recorded gap); the capability
  statement's counts. Requires F1 A or B.

**Dependences.** F2 B needs F1 A or B. F2 A is open under every F1 option.

---

## Not a fork — settled by a standing record (named so the founder sees it)
- **Which element is the canvas.** Architecture `decision/custom-widget-object` («Custom content is an `object`
  whose `data` carries a `CustomWidgetAttr`») and `contract/custom-widget-embed/object-data` settle it: a Dioxus
